## Coastal Wetlands {#am_cw}

Change in the composition of coastal wetlands species over time was
analyzed as a generalized linear model with species group (mangroves and
associates, marsh, marsh succulents, and invasive plants) and species as
independent variables. The models were only run for managed areas that
had at least five years of data in the time series.

Change in the percent cover of coastal wetlands over time were analyzed
as linear mixed models with the following species groups and species:
mangroves and associates (*Avicennia germinans*, *Rhizophora mangle*,
*Laguncularia racemosa* and *Conocarpus erectus*); marsh (*Spartina
alterniflora* [also known as *Sporobolus alterniflorus*], *Spartina
patens*, *Spartina bakeri*, *Distichlis* spp., *Sporobolus* spp.,
*Paspalum* spp. and *Juncus roemerianus*); marsh succulents (*Batis*
spp., *Salicornia* spp., *Sarcocornia* spp., *Blutaparon* spp.,
*Sesuvium* spp., *Suaeda* spp., *Limonium* spp); and invasive plants
(*Schinus terebinthifolia* [also known as *Schinus terebinthifolius*]).
The models treated sample locations as a random effect to account for
the fact that the locations sampled in a managed area in any given year
represent only a handful of the many possible sampling locations. The
models were only run for managed areas that had at least five years of
data in the time series.
